title: React Native's New Architecture: Why It Matters

scenes.line1: Why did React Native need an upgrade?
scenes.say: Ever wonder why React Native apps used to lag or feel sluggish? Let's break down what changed—and why it matters.

scenes.label: Bridge
scenes.sub: Messages passed between JavaScript and native code.
scenes.say: Originally, React Native used something called the bridge. It sent messages between JavaScript and native code, but that process was slow and could block your UI.

scenes.label: JSI
scenes.sub: Direct, synchronous access to native APIs.
scenes.say: The new architecture brings in the JavaScript Interface. Now, JavaScript can talk to native APIs directly and instantly. No more waiting in line.

scenes.label: Fabric
scenes.sub: Modern UI manager for faster, concurrent updates.
scenes.say: Fabric is the new UI manager. It updates your app's interface faster and handles complex layouts way better, especially when lots is happening at once.
Bottom line: the bridge slowed things down. JSI and Fabric make your app feel snappy, with smoother animations and less lag.

scenes.question: Is the bridge still used in the new architecture?
scenes.right: No, JSI replaces the bridge for most native calls.
scenes.say: Interview trap: Don't say the bridge is still the main way JavaScript talks to native code. JSI takes over for most of that now.
